test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 14 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following sentences about money is INCORRECT?

options.text: Money acts as a convenient unit of account.
The value of all goods and services cannot be expressed in monetary units.
Economic exchanges without the mediation of money are referred to as barter exchanges
The first and foremost role of money is that it acts as a medium of exchange.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The value of all goods and services cannot be expressed in monetary units.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The value of all goods and services can be expressed in monetary units.**
 
• For example:
 
 
• t**he value of a certain wristwatch is Rs 500** which **means that the wristwatch can be exchanged for 500 units of money**, where a unit of money is a rupee in this case.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Money **also acts as a **convenient unit of account.**

 
 
• If the price of a pencil is Rs 2 and that of a pen is Rs 10 we can calculate the relative price of a pen with respect to a pencil, viz. a pen is worth 10 ÷ 2 = 5 pencils.
 
• The same notion** can be used to calculate the value of money itself with respect to other commodities.**
 
• In the above example, a rupee is worth 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5 pencil or 1 ÷ 10 = 0.1 pen.
 
 
 
• **The first and foremost role of money is that it acts as a medium of exchange.**
 
 
• ​Barter exchanges become extremely difficult in a large economy** because of the high costs people would have to incur looking for suitable persons to exchange their surpluses.**
 
• To smoothen the transaction,** an intermediate good is necessary which is acceptable to both parties.**
 
• Such a good is called money.
 
 
 
• **Economic exchanges without the mediation of money are referred to as barter exchanges**
 
 
• ​A barter system refers to a **system in which goods are exchanged for other goods.**
 
 

2b
